traps.name: QGA Greedy ...b5 Trap (Qf3)
traps.description: When Black tries to hold the c4 gambit pawn with ...b5, the central diagonal becomes vulnerable. White invites with a4; if Black defends with ...c6 instead of ...a6, the axb5 cxb5 sequence opens the a8-h1 diagonal and Qf3 wins the rook on a8. The reason White plays the Queen's Gambit: Black usually shouldn't try to hold the pawn — and when they do, tactics like this punish it.
traps.how_to_avoid: Answer a4 with ...a6 instead of ...c6. The a-pawn supports b5 without opening a diagonal to the rook.
traps.success_message: QGA Greedy ...b5 Trap. axb5 cxb5 opens the a8-h1 diagonal; Qf3 wins the rook on a8.

steps.explanation: The greedy defense. Black tries to hold b5 with the c-pawn, but this opens the a8-h1 diagonal. ...a6 was the safer try.
White captures, threatening b5 again — Black has no choice but to recapture.

Wins the rook on a8 along the open diagonal. The c4 gambit pawn was never worth the structural damage.
Black develops, but no piece can close the a8-h1 diagonal in time.
White's queen reaches a8 and captures the rook.
